key_idea: Build the universal cover inductively, one scale at a time. At each scale an equivariant path of positive-Ricci metrics on S^3×S^3 untwists a (1,k)-Hopf circle action into a (1,0)-action, so successive finite cyclic generators of Γ ≤ Q/Z can be glued in while keeping Ric ≥ 0.
reason: The central device is genuinely clever and topologically well motivated. It uses a nontrivial equivariant mapping class of S^3×S^3, realized through a positive-Ricci path, to rotate the action at infinity so that the next root can be adjoined. That idea is buried under a long multi-stage gluing construction (X_1 through X_7, A_1 through tilde A), doubly warped product and submersion curvature estimates, and a detailed scale-by-scale analysis, so the reason the result holds is only partly visible through the bookkeeping.
recognized: Bruè–Naber–Semola, 'Fundamental groups and the Milnor conjecture' (counterexample: a 7-manifold with Ric ≥ 0 and infinitely generated fundamental group)
